Add a new function in class `RunContext` of `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/_run_context.py`, after `RunContext.tools`. Its signature and description:

```
def tool_name_for_kind(self, kind: _messages.ToolKindLike) -> str | None:
```

The name of the tool with this [`tool_kind`][pydantic_ai.tools.ToolDefinition.tool_kind] in the current run step, or `None` if there is none.

        Instructions and tool results can use it to name a tool without hard-coding a name that
        may have been changed or prefixed (for example by [`PrefixTools`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.PrefixTools]).

        It reads the same tools as [`tools`][pydantic_ai.tools.RunContext.tools], so a tool hidden by
        deferred loading counts, keeping instructions that name it stable when it is revealed, and a
        tool left out by [`unless_tool_kind`][pydantic_ai.tools.ToolDefinition.unless_tool_kind] doesn't.
        When several tools have the kind, it returns the first in the order of
        [`tools`][pydantic_ai.tools.RunContext.tools], which is the order the step's toolsets list
        them in, so the answer is stable from step to step; iterate `tools` to see them all.

        The step's tools are resolved before its instructions are rendered, so instruction functions,
        model request hooks and tools all see the current step. Inside `get_tools` or a `prepare_tools`
        hook they are still being resolved: there it answers from the previous step, or returns `None`
        on the first. Inside a Temporal activity, where the tool manager isn't attached, it answers from a
        snapshot taken when the activity was dispatched; anywhere else without a tool manager it returns `None`.

        Args:
            kind: The [`ToolKind`][pydantic_ai.messages.ToolKind], or its id.

async def consume_event_stream(
    *,
    run_context: RunContext[Any],
    stream: AsyncIterable[ModelResponseStreamEvent],
    handler: EventStreamHandler[Any] | None,
) -> None:
docstring:
Consume a live model stream inside a durable-execution boundary.

    If a handler is provided, it consumes the live stream inside the boundary. Any
    events it leaves unconsumed are drained, so the stream's final response is complete.
    The events aren't shipped back to the workflow, which replays the final response instead.

    Args:
        run_context: The current agent run context.
        stream: The live model stream.
        handler: Optional handler to run inside the durable boundary.

signature: def _find_prompt_part(ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT], messages: Sequence[ModelMessage]) -> UserPromptPart | None:
docstring:
The user's prompt for this run, as it appears in this request.

    That is the most recent `UserPromptPart` in the run's history, `ctx.messages`. `messages` is
    this request's copy of the history, where an outer capability can add a `UserPromptPart` for
    this request only (`SystemReminders`, `Planning` and `Memory` append one to the last request).
    That part is not the user's prompt, so the prompt is found by identity: the guard neither
    screens nor overwrites the added part. A prompt an outer capability rewrote in place is still
    the same object, so the guard reads the rewritten text.

    When a capability replaced the prompt with a copy, the copy is found by `_find_copy` in the
    most recent message holding a part with the prompt's timestamp, wherever other parts or
    messages were put around it, so neither a message appended for this request nor history
    trimmed from the start moves it. Only when no part can be told to be the copy, because the
    request was rebuilt, is the most recent part in `messages` used.

Add a new function in `src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/guardrails/_capability.py`, after `_require_prompt_text`. Its signature and description:

```
def _find_prompt_part(ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT], messages: Sequence[ModelMessage]) -> UserPromptPart | None:
```

The user's prompt for this run, as it appears in this request.

    That is the most recent `UserPromptPart` in the run's history, `ctx.messages`. `messages` is
    this request's copy of the history, where an outer capability can add a `UserPromptPart` for
    this request only (`SystemReminders`, `Planning` and `Memory` append one to the last request).
    That part is not the user's prompt, so the prompt is found by identity: the guard neither
    screens nor overwrites the added part. A prompt an outer capability rewrote in place is still
    the same object, so the guard reads the rewritten text.

    When a capability replaced the prompt with a copy, the copy is found by `_find_copy` in the
    most recent message holding a part with the prompt's timestamp, wherever other parts or
    messages were put around it, so neither a message appended for this request nor history
    trimmed from the start moves it. Only when no part can be told to be the copy, because the
    request was rebuilt, is the most recent part in `messages` used.

Implement it so the project's tests pass. When your changes are complete, call done.

        `provider_details`. Keep it in the message history: later requests send it back in place of the messages
        before it, with the `compact-2026-09-04` beta that it needs. Only Claude models that support on-demand
        compaction accept the block.

        output's `output_config.format`, the `remaining` task budget and `anthropic_context_management`. A forcing
        `tool_choice` is relaxed to `auto`, and the calls of a trailing response that has no tool results yet are
        dropped. Images and documents in the summarized messages don't survive compaction.

            request_context: The model request context containing messages, settings, and parameters.
            instructions: Optional focus for the summary, such as what to keep. Anthropic replaces its whole
                summarization prompt with the instructions it's given, so the focus is sent inside a full
                summarization prompt rather than on its own. On OpenAI, `instructions` replaces the agent's
                instructions for the compaction request instead.

                [`anthropic_supports_on_demand_compaction`][pydantic_ai.profiles.anthropic.AnthropicModelProfile.anthropic_supports_on_demand_compaction]
                profile flag.

@@ -0,0 +1,387 @@
+"""Tests for `AnthropicModel.compact_messages`, Anthropic's on-demand compaction.
+
+The recorded tests compact a short synthetic conversation of project decisions on `claude-haiku-5-5`, pin the
+compaction request as the model built it (via `request_capture`, which also sees the beta header the cassettes
+strip), and send the returned block back on later requests to the same model and to `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations as _annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import pytest
+
+from pydantic_ai import (
+    Agent,
+    ModelRequest,
+    ModelResponse,
+    RequestUsage,
+    TextPart,
+    ToolCallPart,
+    UnexpectedModelBehavior,
+    UserError,
+)
+from pydantic_ai._context_size import context_tokens
+from pydantic_ai.messages import CompactionPart, ModelMessage
+from pydantic_ai.models import ModelRequestContext, ModelRequestParameters
+from pydantic_ai.output import OutputObjectDefinition
+from pydantic_ai.tools import ToolDefinition
+
+from ..._inline_snapshot import snapshot
+from ...conftest import IsStr, RequestCapture, try_import
+from ..conftest import message_shape
+
+with try_import() as imports_successful:
+    from anthropic import (
+        AsyncAnthropic,
+        AsyncAnthropicBedrock,
+        AsyncAnthropicBedrockMantle,
+        AsyncAnthropicFoundry,
+        AsyncAnthropicVertex,
+    )
+
+    from pydantic_ai.models.anthropic import AnthropicModel, AnthropicModelSettings
+    from pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic import AnthropicProvider
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic import AsyncAnthropicClient
+
+    from ..conftest import AnthropicModelFactory
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.skipif(not imports_successful(), reason='anthropic not installed'),
+    pytest.mark.vcr,
+]
+
+_DECISIONS = [
+    ('DB-1', 'Use PostgreSQL 17 as the primary database', 'the team already runs it in two other services'),
+    ('FE-1', 'Use React 19 for the web client', 'server components cut the bundle size for the dashboard'),
+    ('DB-2', 'Put pgbouncer in front of PostgreSQL', 'the worker fleet opens too many short-lived connections'),
+    ('OPS-1', 'Deploy on Fly.io in two regions', 'latency for European customers was over 300 ms'),
+    ('DB-3', 'Take nightly base backups to S3 with 30-day retention', 'compliance asked for a month of history'),
+    ('FE-2', 'Use Tailwind CSS for styling', 'the design system tokens map onto its theme config'),
+    ('OPS-2', 'Ship logs and traces to Logfire', 'one place to debug both the API and the workers'),
+    ('DB-4', 'Run migrations with Alembic in a pre-deploy step', 'a failed migration must block the release'),
+]
+
+
+def _conversation() -> list[ModelMessage]:
+    """A synthetic conversation recording project decisions, ending with a request that is still open."""
+    messages: list[ModelMessage] = []
+    for decision_id, decision, reason in _DECISIONS:
+        messages.append(
+            ModelRequest.user_text_prompt(
+                f'Record project decision {decision_id}: {decision}. The reason: {reason}. '
+                'Acknowledge it in one sentence.',
+                instructions='You keep track of the decisions for a web application project.',
+            )
+        )
+        messages.append(
+            ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart(f'Recorded {decision_id}: {decision}.')], provider_name='anthropic')
+        )
+    messages.append(
+        ModelRequest.user_text_prompt(
+            'Next, help me pick a job queue for the workers.',
+            instructions='You keep track of the decisions for a web application project.',
+        )
+    )
+    return messages
+
+
+def _context(
+    model: AnthropicModel,
+    messages: list[ModelMessage],
+    model_settings: AnthropicModelSettings | None = None,
+    model_request_parameters: ModelRequestParameters | None = None,
+) -> ModelRequestContext:
+    return ModelRequestContext(
+        model=model,
+        messages=messages,
+        model_settings=model_settings,
+        model_request_parameters=model_request_parameters or ModelRequestParameters(),
+    )
+
+
+def _betas(request_capture: RequestCapture, index: int) -> list[str]:
+    return sorted(request_capture.headers[index].get('anthropic-beta', '').split(','))
+
+
+async def test_compact_messages(
+    allow_model_requests: None, anthropic_model: AnthropicModelFactory, request_capture: RequestCapture
+):
+    """The response holds the signed summary, and its usage is the compaction iteration's.
+
+    Without `max_tokens`, the model's maximum output is sent, so the SDK has the request streamed behind the scenes
+    and the block arrives in a `content_block_start` event. Anthropic reports the usage of a compaction request in
+    `usage.iterations` only, with the top-level counts at zero.
+    """
+    model = anthropic_model('claude-haiku-5-5', capture=True)
+
+    response = await model.compact_messages(_context(model, _conversation()))
+
+    assert response.parts == snapshot(
+        [
+            CompactionPart(
+                content=IsStr(regex=r'(?s).*PostgreSQL.*Tailwind.*'),
+                provider_name='anthropic',
+                provider_details={'signature': IsStr()},
+            )
+        ]
+    )
+    assert response.finish_reason == 'stop'
+    assert response.provider_details == snapshot({'finish_reason': 'compaction'})
+    assert response.usage == snapshot(
+        RequestUsage(
+            details={
+                'input_tokens': 0,
+                'output_tokens': 0,
+                'cache_creation_input_tokens': 0,
+                'cache_read_input_tokens': 0,
+                'message_iterations': 0,
+                'compaction_iterations': 1,
+                'compaction_input_tokens': 790,
+                'compaction_output_tokens': 859,
+            },
+            input_tokens=790,
+            output_tokens=859,
+        )
+    )
+
+    # The usage is the summarized conversation, but the context the response leaves behind is the summary alone,
+    # so a size trigger that reads it doesn't fire again right after compacting.
+    assert context_tokens(response) == response.usage.output_tokens
+
+    body = request_capture.body('/v1/messages')
+    assert body['compaction'] == snapshot({'type': 'summarize'})
+    assert 'context_management' not in body
+    assert _betas(request_capture, 0) == snapshot(['compact-2026-09-04'])
+
+
+async def test_compact_messages_with_focus(
+    allow_model_requests: None, anthropic_model: AnthropicModelFactory, request_capture: RequestCapture
+):
+    """A focus is sent inside a full summarization prompt, since Anthropic's own prompt is replaced entirely.
+
+    The effort is one of the settings a compaction request keeps, as it would be sent on any other request.
+    """
+    model = anthropic_model('claude-haiku-5-5', capture=True)
+
+    response = await model.compact_messages(
+        _context(model, _conversation(), AnthropicModelSettings(max_tokens=4096, anthropic_effort='low')),
+        instructions='Only the database decisions; leave out everything else.',
+    )
+
+    compaction = response.parts[0]
+    assert isinstance(compaction, CompactionPart)
+    assert compaction.content is not None
+    assert 'PostgreSQL' in compaction.content
+    assert 'Tailwind' not in compaction.content
+    # Without streaming, the usage comes from the compaction iteration too.
+    assert response.usage.input_tokens == response.usage.details['compaction_input_tokens'] > 0
+    assert response.usage.output_tokens == response.usage.details['compaction_output_tokens'] > 0
+
+    body = request_capture.body('/v1/messages')
+    assert body['output_config'] == snapshot({'effort': 'low'})
+    assert body['compaction'] == snapshot(
+        {
+            'type': 'summarize',
+            'instructions': """\
+Write a summary of the conversation so far. It replaces the conversation: whoever continues it sees only your summary, so anything you leave out is lost.
+
+Keep:
+- the user's goals, requests and constraints, and how they changed;
+- the decisions made and why, with exact names, identifiers, values, file paths and commands;
+- the tool results that later work depends on;
+- what is done, what is in progress and what comes next, including any request still waiting for an answer.
+
+Write it as notes for whoever continues the conversation. Don't answer the latest request, and don't add anything the conversation doesn't contain.
+
+The summary should focus on the following. Where it conflicts with the guidance above, follow it:
+<focus>
+Only the database decisions; leave out everything else.
+</focus>\
+""",
+        }
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.moves_cache_prefix(reason='replaces the conversation with its compaction block on purpose')
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('replay_model_name', ['claude-haiku-5-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6'])
+async def test_compact_messages_replay(
+    allow_model_requests: None,
+    anthropic_model: AnthropicModelFactory,
+    request_capture: RequestCapture,
+    replay_model_name: str,
+):
+    """A later request sends the block back in place of the conversation, with the beta it needs.
+
+    It's billed for the summary rather than the conversation, on the model that compacted and on another
+    compaction-capable one. The block isn't combined with the threshold compaction edit, which Anthropic rejects
+    alongside a signed block.
+    """
+    model = anthropic_model('claude-haiku-5-5', capture=True)
+    conversation = _conversation()
+    compacted = await model.compact_messages(_context(model, conversation, AnthropicModelSettings(max_tokens=4096)))
+
+    agent = Agent(
+        anthropic_model(replay_model_name, capture=True), model_settings=AnthropicModelSettings(max_tokens=512)
+    )
+    result = await agent.run(
+        'Which database did we pick, and what sits in front of it? Answer in one sentence.',
+        message_history=[*conversation, compacted],
+    )
+
+    assert 'pgbouncer' in result.output.lower()
+    body = request_capture.body('/v1/messages', index=1)
+    assert message_shape(body) == snapshot([('assistant', ['compaction']), ('user', ['text'])])
+    assert 'context_management' not in body
+    assert 'compact-2026-09-04' in _betas(request_capture, 1)
+    assert result.usage.input_tokens < compacted.usage.input_tokens
+
+
+@pytest.mark.moves_cache_prefix(reason='replaces the conversation with its compaction block on purpose')
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ('transport', 'model_name'),
+    [('bedrock', 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5'), ('mantle', 'anthropic.claude-opus-5-5')],
+)
+async def test_compact_messages_on_aws(
+    allow_model_requests: None,
+    request_capture: RequestCapture,
+    request: pytest.FixtureRequest,
+    transport: str,
+    model_name: str,
+):
+    """Both Amazon Bedrock APIs compact, and accept the block back, although Anthropic's docs don't list Bedrock.
+
+    The legacy InvokeModel API carries the beta in the body's `anthropic_beta`, the AWS-operated Messages API
+    (`AsyncAnthropicBedrockMantle`) in the `anthropic-beta` header, on the compaction request and on the request that
+    sends the block back. The Messages API serves neither Claude Haiku 5.5 nor Sonnet 4.6, so it's recorded with
+    Claude Opus 5.5.
+    """
+    client = request.getfixturevalue(f'anthropic_{"bedrock" if transport == "bedrock" else "bedrock_mantle"}_client')
+    model = AnthropicModel(model_name, provider=AnthropicProvider(anthropic_client=client))
+    conversation = _conversation()
+
+    compacted = await model.compact_messages(_context(model, conversation, AnthropicModelSettings(max_tokens=4096)))
+    result = await Agent(model, model_settings=AnthropicModelSettings(max_tokens=512)).run(
+        'Which database did we pick, and what sits in front of it? Answer in one sentence.',
+        message_history=[*conversation, compacted],
+    )
+
+    assert compacted.parts == snapshot(
+        [
+            CompactionPart(
+                content=IsStr(regex=r'(?s).*PostgreSQL.*'),
+                provider_name='anthropic',
+                provider_details={'signature': IsStr()},
+            )
+        ]
+    )
+    assert 'pgbouncer' in result.output.lower()
+    compaction_body, replay_body = request_capture.bodies()
+    assert compaction_body['compaction'] == snapshot({'type': 'summarize'})
+    assert message_shape(replay_body) == snapshot([('assistant', ['compaction']), ('user', ['text'])])
+    for index, body in enumerate((compaction_body, replay_body)):
+        if transport == 'bedrock':
+            assert body['anthropic_beta'] == snapshot(['compact-2026-09-04'])
+        else:
+            assert _betas(request_capture, index) == snapshot(['compact-2026-09-04'])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    'client',
+    [
+        pytest.param(lambda: AsyncAnthropic(api_key='x'), id='anthropic'),
+        pytest.param(lambda: AsyncAnthropicBedrock(api_key='x', aws_region='us-east-1'), id='bedrock'),
+        pytest.param(lambda: AsyncAnthropicBedrockMantle(api_key='x', aws_region='us-east-1'), id='mantle'),
+        pytest.param(lambda: AsyncAnthropicVertex(project_id='p', region='global', access_token='x'), id='vertex'),
+        pytest.param(lambda: AsyncAnthropicFoundry(api_key='x', resource='r'), id='foundry'),
+    ],
+)
+def test_compact_messages_supported_on_every_client(client: Callable[[], AsyncAnthropicClient]):
+    """No client narrows the flag, as none has been seen to reject on-demand compaction.
+
+    The direct API and both Bedrock clients are recorded above. Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry are documented as
+    supported, but not recorded: our credentials reach no Claude model there.
+    """
+    model = AnthropicModel('claude-haiku-5-5', provider=AnthropicProvider(anthropic_client=client()))
+
+    assert model.profile.get('anthropic_supports_on_demand_compaction') is True
+
+
+async def test_compact_messages_settles_rejected_parameters(
+    allow_model_requests: None, anthropic_model: AnthropicModelFactory, request_capture: RequestCapture
+):
+    """What Anthropic rejects on a compaction request is left out, and a forcing `tool_choice` is relaxed.
+
+    The trailing tool call has no result yet, which Anthropic rejects too, so it's dropped along with
+    `stop_sequences`, structured output's `output_config.format`, the `remaining` task budget and
+    `anthropic_context_management`. The rest of the request stays as it would otherwise be sent.
+    """
+    model = anthropic_model('claude-haiku-5-5', capture=True)
+    messages = [
+        *_conversation(),
+        ModelResponse(
+            parts=[
+                TextPart('Let me look up the queue options.'),
+                ToolCallPart('list_job_queues', {}, tool_call_id='toolu_01'),
+            ],
+            provider_name='anthropic',
+        ),
+    ]
+    settings = AnthropicModelSettings(
+        max_tokens=4096,
+        stop_sequences=['END'],
+        tool_choice='required',
+        anthropic_task_budget={'type': 'tokens', 'total': 100_000, 'remaining': 50_000},
+        anthropic_context_management={'edits': [{'type': 'clear_tool_uses_20250919'}]},
+    )
+    parameters = ModelRequestParameters(
+        function_tools=[ToolDefinition(name='list_job_queues', description='List the job queue options.')],
+        output_mode='native',
+        output_object=OutputObjectDefinition(
+            json_schema={'type': 'object', 'properties': {'queue': {'type': 'string'}}, 'required': ['queue']}
+        ),
+    )
+
+    response = await model.compact_messages(_context(model, messages, settings, parameters))
+
+    assert isinstance(response.parts[0], CompactionPart)
+    body = request_capture.body('/v1/messages')
+    assert {key: body.get(key) for key in ('tool_choice', 'output_config', 'stop_sequences', 'context_management')} == (
+        snapshot(
+            {
+                'tool_choice': {'type': 'auto'},
+                'output_config': {'task_budget': {'type': 'tokens', 'total': 100000}},
+                'stop_sequences': None,
+                'context_management': None,
+            }
+        )
+    )
+    assert message_shape(body)[-2:] == snapshot([('user', ['text']), ('assistant', ['text'])])
+
+
+async def test_compact_messages_without_summary(
+    allow_model_requests: None, anthropic_model: AnthropicModelFactory, request_capture: RequestCapture
+):
+    """A 200 without a block is an error, not an empty summary that would drop the history it can't replace."""
+    model = anthropic_model('claude-haiku-5-5', capture=True)
+
+    with pytest.raises(UnexpectedModelBehavior) as exc_info:
+        await model.compact_messages(_context(model, _conversation(), AnthropicModelSettings(max_tokens=5)))
+
+    assert str(exc_info.value) == snapshot(
+        "Anthropic returned no compaction summary (stop reason 'max_tokens'). Raise `max_tokens` to leave room for the summary."
+    )
+
+
+async def test_compact_messages_unsupported_model(allow_model_requests: None, anthropic_model: AnthropicModelFactory):
+    """A model without on-demand compaction raises before sending, rather than with the API's 400.
+
+    No request is sent, so there is nothing to record.
+    """
+    model = anthropic_model('claude-haiku-4-5')
+
+    with pytest.raises(UserError, match="'claude-haiku-4-5' does not support on-demand compaction"):
+        await model.compact_messages(_context(model, _conversation()))

prompt:
Add a new function in class `AnthropicModel` of `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/models/anthropic/__init__.py`, after `AnthropicModel.request`. Its signature and description:

```
async def compact_messages(
        self,
        request_context: ModelRequestContext,
        *,
        instructions: str | None = None,
    ) -> ModelResponse:
```

Compact messages with Anthropic's on-demand compaction.

        This sends the conversation to the Messages API with the `compaction` parameter, which summarizes it instead
        of replying. It reads the conversation's prompt cache, like any other request with the same prefix. The
        returned `ModelResponse` holds a single `CompactionPart` with the readable summary, and its signature in
        `provider_details`. Keep it in the message history: later requests send it back in place of the messages
        before it, with the `compact-2026-09-04` beta that it needs. Only Claude models that support on-demand
        compaction accept the block.

        The parameters Anthropic rejects on a compaction request are left out of it: `stop_sequences`, structured
        output's `output_config.format`, the `remaining` task budget and `anthropic_context_management`. A forcing
        `tool_choice` is relaxed to `auto`, and the calls of a trailing response that has no tool results yet are
        dropped. Images and documents in the summarized messages don't survive compaction.

        Args:
            request_context: The model request context containing messages, settings, and parameters.
            instructions: Optional focus for the summary, such as what to keep. Anthropic replaces its whole
                summarization prompt with the instructions it's given, so the focus is sent inside a full
                summarization prompt rather than on its own. On OpenAI, `instructions` replaces the agent's
                instructions for the compaction request instead.

        Returns:
            A `ModelResponse` with a single `CompactionPart` containing the summary.

        Raises:
            UserError: If the model doesn't support on-demand compaction, according to its
                [`anthropic_supports_on_demand_compaction`][pydantic_ai.profiles.anthropic.AnthropicModelProfile.anthropic_supports_on_demand_compaction]
                profile flag.
            UnexpectedModelBehavior: If Anthropic returns no summary, for example when `max_tokens` cuts it off.

Implement it so the project's tests pass. When your changes are complete, call done.

subject: Keep the prompt cache when changing thinking effort mid-conversation on OpenRouter, via its `configuration_update` system message (#11426)
docstring:
Decide whether this request sends effort changes as `configuration_update` messages.

        It does when the history holds a mid-conversation change (a `ModelSettingsDeltaPart` that
        `prepare_messages` kept for this model) and no explicit `openrouter_reasoning` or `openai_reasoning_effort`
        rules it out: those are sent as is. The request then keeps the window's opening effort as its
        `reasoning.effort`, so its prefix matches the earlier requests'. Otherwise the parts are removed and the
        current effort goes out as `reasoning.effort`, as it would without them.

        Runs before `prepare_request` turns the unified `thinking` setting into `reasoning`, so it pins the opening
        effort as the request's `thinking`.

+async def test_openrouter_effort_change_keeps_the_cache(
+    allow_model_requests: None,
+    openrouter_api_key: str,
+    request_capture: RequestCapture,
+    model_name: str,
+    expected_request: Any,
+):
+    """The second run sends the change as a content-less `system` message and reads the first run's prefix from cache.
+
+    Sent as the request-level `reasoning.effort` instead, the change read 0 of 8,058 prompt tokens from cache on
+    `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` (recorded 2026-10-26). OpenRouter translates the message to the routed model's own form.
+    """
+    provider = OpenRouterProvider(api_key=openrouter_api_key, http_client=request_capture.http_client(timeout=120))
+    agent = Agent(OpenRouterModel(model_name, provider=provider), instructions=_PREFIX)
+    settings = OpenRouterModelSettings(openrouter_cache_instructions=True, openrouter_cache_messages=True)
+    first = await agent.run('Where is item 12?', model_settings={**settings, 'thinking': 'low'})
+    second = await agent.run(
+        'And item 40?', message_history=first.all_messages(), model_settings={**settings, 'thinking': 'high'}
+    )
+
+    _, second_request = request_capture.bodies()
+    # The instructions are left out: they're the long cached prefix.
+    messages = cast(list[Any], second_request['messages'])[1:]
+    assert {'reasoning': second_request['reasoning'], 'messages': messages} == expected_request
+    assert second.response.usage.cache_read_tokens >= first.response.usage.input_tokens - 100
+

subject: Keep `ToolOutputLimits` bands largest-first after `combine`, with the later band winning a shared threshold (#11453)
signature: def combine(cls, capabilities: Sequence[AbstractCapability[AgentDepsT]]) -> AbstractCapability[AgentDepsT]:

        `_store`, `_bands`, and `_per_tool` are derived in `__post_init__`, which merging skips, so
        they are rebuilt from the merged configuration: a merged band list keeps the largest-first
        order a single instance has, and a stated `store` is the one spills go to.

+"""`FallbackCompaction(background_start=...)`: summarize ahead of the trigger, swap the summary in when due."""
+
+import asyncio
+from collections.abc import Generator
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+import anyio
+import pytest
+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import ReadableSpan, TracerProvider
+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter
+
+from pydantic_ai import Agent, ModelHTTPError, RunContext, UserError
+from pydantic_ai.capabilities import AbstractCapability
+from pydantic_ai.messages import (
+    CompactionPart,
+    ModelMessage,
+    ModelRequest,
+    ModelResponse,
+    TextPart,
+    ToolCallPart,
+    ToolReturnPart,
+)
+from pydantic_ai.models import ModelRequestContext
+from pydantic_ai.models.function import AgentInfo, FunctionModel
+from pydantic_ai.models.instrumented import InstrumentationSettings
+from pydantic_ai.usage import RequestUsage
+from pydantic_ai_harness.compaction import FallbackCompaction, SlidingWindowCompaction, SummarizingCompaction
+from pydantic_ai_harness.compaction._fallback_compaction import MAX_BACKGROUND_COMPACTIONS
+
+READINESS_WAIT_TIMEOUT = 10
+
+TRIGGER = 2_000
+"""`max_tokens` of every chain here; `background_start=0.5` starts the summary above 1,000."""
+
+OLD = 'old ' * 4_000
+"""The opening prompt: about 4,000 tokens of text, which the summary replaces."""
+
+OVER = 'more ' * 800
+"""A prompt of about 1,000 tokens: after a 1,150-token response, it takes the next request over the trigger."""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Summarizer:
+    """The summary model: waits for `release`, then answers, raises while `failures` remain, or is cancelled."""
+
+    release: asyncio.Event = field(default_factory=asyncio.Event)
+    started: asyncio.Event = field(default_factory=asyncio.Event)
+    failures: int = 0
+    cancel: bool = False
+    calls: int = 0
+    finished: int = 0
+    cancelled: int = 0
+
+    async def __call__(self, messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> ModelResponse:
+        self.calls += 1
+        self.started.set()
+        try:
+            await self.release.wait()
+        except asyncio.CancelledError:
+            self.cancelled += 1
+            raise
+        if self.cancel:
+            self.cancel = False
+            raise asyncio.CancelledError
+        if self.failures:
+            self.failures -= 1
+            raise ModelHTTPError(status_code=503, model_name='summarizer', body=None)
+        self.finished += 1
+        return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart(f'summary {self.calls}')])
+
+    async def wait_started(self) -> None:
+        with anyio.fail_after(READINESS_WAIT_TIMEOUT):
+            await self.started.wait()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Main:
+    """The conversation's model. Each response reports `input_tokens`, the context size the trigger reads."""
+
+    input_tokens: list[int]
+    tool_first: bool = False
+    answer_after: Summarizer | None = None
+    """When set, the final answer waits until this summarizer has started."""
+
+    async def __call__(self, messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> ModelResponse:
+        usage = RequestUsage(input_tokens=self.input_tokens.pop(0))
+        last = messages[-1]
+        if self.tool_first and not any(isinstance(part, ToolReturnPart) for part in last.parts):
+            return ModelResponse(parts=[ToolCallPart('lookup', {}, tool_call_id='call-1')], usage=usage)
+        if self.answer_after is not None:
+            await self.answer_after.wait_started()
+        return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart('done')], usage=usage)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Requesting(AbstractCapability[None]):
+    """Sets `event` as a request starts, before the compaction listed after it runs."""
+
+    event: asyncio.Event = field(default_factory=asyncio.Event)
+
+    async def before_model_request(
+        self, ctx: RunContext[None], request_context: ModelRequestContext
+    ) -> ModelRequestContext:
+        self.event.set()
+        return request_context
+
+    async def wait(self) -> None:
+        with anyio.fail_after(READINESS_WAIT_TIMEOUT):
+            await self.event.wait()
+
+
+def chain(summarizer: Summarizer, *, background_start: float | None = 0.5) -> FallbackCompaction[None]:
+    return FallbackCompaction(
+        fallback_chain=[
+            SummarizingCompaction(
+                model=FunctionModel(summarizer, model_name='summarizer'),
+                max_messages=1,
+                keep_messages=1,
+                preserve_first_user_message=False,
+            ),
+            SlidingWindowCompaction(max_messages=1, keep_messages=1),
+        ],
+        max_tokens=TRIGGER,
+        background_start=background_start,
+    )
+
+
+def agent(
+    main: Main,
+    compaction: FallbackCompaction[None],
+    name: str = 'main',
+    *,
+    before: tuple[AbstractCapability[None], ...] = (),
+) -> Agent[None, str]:
+    built = Agent(FunctionModel(main, model_name=name), deps_type=type(None), capabilities=[*before, compaction])
+
+    @built.tool_plain
+    def lookup() -> str:
+        return 'found it'
+
+    return built
+
+
+def opening(input_tokens: int) -> list[ModelMessage]:
+    """A first turn, from an earlier run, whose response reported `input_tokens`."""
+    return [
+        ModelRequest.user_text_prompt(OLD),
+        ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart('ok')], usage=RequestUsage(input_tokens=input_tokens)),
+    ]
+
+
+def summaries(messages: list[ModelMessage]) -> list[str | None]:
+    return [
+        part.content
+        for message in messages
+        if isinstance(message, ModelRequest)
+        for part in message.parts
+        if isinstance(part, CompactionPart)
+    ]
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def traced() -> Generator[InMemorySpanExporter]:
+    spans = InMemorySpanExporter()
+    provider = TracerProvider()
+    provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(spans))
+    Agent.instrument_all(InstrumentationSettings(tracer_provider=provider))
+    try:
+        yield spans
+    finally:
+        Agent.instrument_all(False)
+
+
+def named(spans: InMemorySpanExporter, name: str) -> list[ReadableSpan]:
+    return [span for span in spans.get_finished_spans() if span.name == name]
+
+
+async def start_background(summarizer: Summarizer, compaction: FallbackCompaction[None]) -> list[ModelMessage]:
+    """One run that starts a background summary and ends while it is still being written."""
+    first = await agent(Main([1_150]), compaction).run('next', message_history=opening(1_100), conversation_id='c')
+    await summarizer.wait_started()
+    return first.all_messages()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(('input_tokens', 'starts'), [(990, False), (1_100, True)])
+async def test_starts_above_the_background_threshold_only(input_tokens: int, starts: bool) -> None:

+        'next', message_history=opening(input_tokens), conversation_id='c'
+    )

+    if starts:
+        await summarizer.wait_started()

+    await compaction.aclose()

+async def test_held_summary_swaps_in_and_keeps_what_came_after_verbatim() -> None:
+    summarizer = Summarizer()
+    compaction = chain(summarizer)
+    with traced() as spans:
+        first = await agent(Main([1_150, 1_200], tool_first=True), compaction).run(
+            'next', message_history=opening(1_100), conversation_id='c'
+        )
+        await summarizer.wait_started()
+        assert 'c' in compaction.background_conversations and summarizer.finished == 0
+        # The run called a tool and answered while the summary was still being written.
+        added = first.all_messages()[3:]
+        assert [type(message) for message in added] == [ModelResponse, ModelRequest, ModelResponse]
+        assert first.usage.requests == 2, 'nothing has finished yet to count'
+
+        summarizer.release.set()
+        second = await agent(Main([500]), compaction).run(
+            OVER, message_history=first.all_messages(), conversation_id='c'
+        )
+    summary, kept, *rest = second.all_messages()
+    assert summaries([summary]) == ['summary 1']
+    assert kept == first.all_messages()[2], 'the request the snapshot ended with is the tail the summary kept'
+    assert rest[:3] == added, 'the tool call and its return, added during the summary, are kept verbatim'
+    assert summarizer.calls == 1, 'no second summary: the held one was used'
+    assert 'c' not in compaction.background_conversations
+    assert first.usage.requests == 3, 'the summary request counts toward the run that started it'
+    assert second.usage.requests == 1
+    [background] = named(spans, 'background_compaction')
+    assert dict(background.attributes or {}) == {
+        'compaction.strategy': 'SummarizingCompaction',
+        'compaction.messages_before': 3,
+    }
+    [compacted] = named(spans, 'compact_messages')
+    assert compacted.attributes is not None and compacted.attributes['compaction.background'] == 'used'

+async def test_waits_for_a_summary_still_being_written() -> None:
+    summarizer = Summarizer()
+    compaction = chain(summarizer)
+    history = await start_background(summarizer, compaction)
+    requesting = Requesting()
+    run = asyncio.create_task(
+        agent(Main([500]), compaction, before=(requesting,)).run(OVER, message_history=history, conversation_id='c')
+    )
+    await requesting.wait()

+async def test_cancelled_wait_leaves_the_summary_for_later() -> None:

+    compaction = chain(summarizer)
+    history = await start_background(summarizer, compaction)

+
+    async def inspect_each_prompt(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> AsyncIterator[str | DeltaToolCalls]:
+        if any(isinstance(part, UserPromptPart) for part in messages[-1].parts):
+            yield {0: DeltaToolCall(name='inspect', json_args='{}')}
+        else:

+    @child.tool
+    async def inspect(ctx: RunContext[object]) -> str:

+        started.set()
+        await finish.wait()
+        return 'inspected'

+    async def resolve(ctx: RunContext[object], request: DelegationWorkspaceRequest) -> Workspace:
+        return Workspace(LocalWorkspaceBackend(tmp_path / request.directory))

+        async with DelegationTasks(directory=tmp_path / 'tasks').opened() as owner:
+            with owner.bind():

docstring:
The entries of `manifest` that gate review and that a pull request changing `files` touches.

    `read_base` and `read_head` return a core file's source at the pull request's merge base and head. They are
    only called with a path that is both a manifest key and in `files`.

    A removed line is placed in the merge-base source and an added line in the head source, each in the innermost
    definition around it. A line of a `self.name = ...` assignment in a method is also placed in `Class.name`,
    where the generator records an instance attribute. A comment, docstring or blank line changes no behavior and
    is placed nowhere. A change placed in qualname `T` touches entry `Q` when `T == Q` or `T` is nested under `Q`.

    A core file the pull request removes or renames touches all of its entries: the engines import its
    definitions from the path it leaves. So does one whose lines cannot be placed, because GitHub left its patch
    out, the patch does not match the fetched source, or the source does not parse.

subject: Add `manage_message_history` to UI adapters so a server-held history isn't sent to the model twice (#11431)
docstring:
Take the client's new turn under `manage_message_history='server'`, and the stored history it continues.

    The new turn is the client's requests after its last response. When its first message has the UI
    message id of a stored request with a user prompt, the client resubmitted that message, as a
    regenerate, an edit or a retried submit does, and the stored history is cut just before it, so the
    run replaces that turn. Only a user prompt can be resubmitted: a client can't cut the history at any
    other request whose id it knows. The tool results the cut request carries stay, as the server
    recorded them: a run merges the results of the calls before it into the client's next request.

    `regenerate` says the request asks to regenerate an answer, which is only possible for a message
    the stored history holds. When it doesn't, a `UserError` says so rather than adding a turn: the
    server never stored that message, as when its run failed or was stopped and the client retries it,
    or the client holds a different conversation than the server, as a client in a stale tab does.
    Without the client's assistant ids, the two can't be told apart.

    Tool results in the new turn are kept only for calls the stored history's last response is still
    waiting on. Copies of the results kept from the cut request are dropped without a warning, as an
    honest client resubmits them too, and other results with one. Compaction parts are never kept, as
    the client doesn't own the history they would cut off. See `_drop_compaction_parts`.

+def conversation_view(messages: Sequence[ModelMessage]) -> list[str]:
+    """One line per prompt, text, tool call and tool return part in `messages`, as the model is shown them."""
+    view: list[str] = []

+        for part in msg.parts:
+            if isinstance(part, ToolCallPart):
+                view.append(f'call {part.tool_call_id}')
+            elif isinstance(part, ToolReturnPart):
+                view.append(f'return {part.tool_call_id}: {part.content}')
+            elif isinstance(part, (UserPromptPart, SystemPromptPart, TextPart)):  # pragma: no branch
+                view.append(f'{part.part_kind}: {part.content}')

+def server_history_agent(
+    toolsets: Sequence[AbstractToolset[None]] = (),

+    """An agent for the UI adapters' server-held history tests, with the model requests and tool runs it records.
+
+    It calls `get_location` for "where am I?" and the approval-gated `delete_file` for "delete a.txt", and answers
+    `ok` otherwise. Pass the frontend `get_location` tool as `toolsets` for a protocol that doesn't send it.

+    requests: list[list[ModelMessage]] = []
+    deleted: list[str] = []
+
+    async def stream_function(messages: list[ModelMessage], _info: AgentInfo) -> AsyncIterator[DeltaToolCalls | str]:
+        requests.append(messages)
+        last = messages[-1].parts[-1]
+        if isinstance(last, UserPromptPart) and last.content == 'where am I?':
+            yield {0: DeltaToolCall(name='get_location', json_args='{}', tool_call_id='loc-1')}
+        elif isinstance(last, UserPromptPart) and last.content == 'delete a.txt':
+            yield {0: DeltaToolCall(name='delete_file', json_args='{"path": "a.txt"}', tool_call_id='del-1')}
+        else:
+            yield 'ok'

+    agent: Agent[None, str | DeferredToolRequests] = Agent(

+async def _server_history_turn(
+    agent: Agent[None, str | DeferredToolRequests],
+    run_input: SubmitMessage | RegenerateMessage,
+    message_history: list[ModelMessage] | None,
+    sdk_version: Literal[5, 6, 7] = 5,
+) -> list[ModelMessage]:
+    """One request through an endpoint that keeps the history on the server, returning what it persists."""
+    adapter = VercelAIAdapter(agent, run_input, sdk_version=sdk_version, manage_message_history='server')
+    results: list[AgentRunResult[Any]] = []
+    async for _ in adapter.run_stream(message_history=message_history, on_complete=results.append):
+        pass
+    [result] = results
+    return result.all_messages()

Add a new function in `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/ui/_adapter.py`, after `retry_feedback_from_payload`. Its signature and description:

```
def _take_new_turn(
    message_history: Sequence[ModelMessage], client_messages: Sequence[ModelMessage], *, regenerate: bool = False
) -> _ServerHeldTurn:
```

Take the client's new turn under `manage_message_history='server'`, and the stored history it continues.

    The new turn is the client's requests after its last response. When its first message has the UI
    message id of a stored request with a user prompt, the client resubmitted that message, as a
    regenerate, an edit or a retried submit does, and the stored history is cut just before it, so the
    run replaces that turn. Only a user prompt can be resubmitted: a client can't cut the history at any
    other request whose id it knows. The tool results the cut request carries stay, as the server
    recorded them: a run merges the results of the calls before it into the client's next request.

    `regenerate` says the request asks to regenerate an answer, which is only possible for a message
    the stored history holds. When it doesn't, a `UserError` says so rather than adding a turn: the
    server never stored that message, as when its run failed or was stopped and the client retries it,
    or the client holds a different conversation than the server, as a client in a stale tab does.
    Without the client's assistant ids, the two can't be told apart.

    Tool results in the new turn are kept only for calls the stored history's last response is still
    waiting on. Copies of the results kept from the cut request are dropped without a warning, as an
    honest client resubmits them too, and other results with one. Compaction parts are never kept, as
    the client doesn't own the history they would cut off. See `_drop_compaction_parts`.

Implement it so the project's tests pass. When your changes are complete, call done.

+class MarkHistoryPerAttempt(AbstractCapability[None]):
+    """Records each attempt on the latest request through `ctx.messages`, then asks for a second attempt."""
+
+    async def prepare_model_request(
+        self, ctx: RunContext[None], request_context: ModelRequestContext
+    ) -> ModelRequestContext:
+        index = max(i for i, message in enumerate(ctx.messages) if isinstance(message, ModelRequest))
+        request = ctx.messages[index]
+        assert isinstance(request, ModelRequest)
+        marks = (request.metadata or {}).get('attempts', [])
+        ctx.messages[index] = replace(request, metadata={'attempts': [*marks, request_context.attempt]})
+        if request_context.attempt == 1:
+            raise RetryModelRequest()
+        return request_context

+def streaming_model(respond: Callable[[list[ModelMessage], AgentInfo], ModelResponse]) -> FunctionModel:
+    """Supply streamed responses for Coder's argument-repair capability."""
+
+    async def stream(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> AsyncIterator[str | DeltaToolCalls]:
+        for part in respond(messages, info).parts:
+            if isinstance(part, TextPart):
+                yield part.content
+            elif isinstance(part, ToolCallPart):
+                yield {0: DeltaToolCall(name=part.tool_name, json_args=json.dumps(part.args_as_dict()))}
+
+    return FunctionModel(respond, stream_function=stream)

+async def test_safe_output_past_its_limit_is_answered_and_no_longer_offered(
+    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    """gh-aw rejects a `noop` past its per-run limit; with one tool retry, the second rejection ended the run.
+
+    UI Security Review's model kept calling `noop` past its limit while it stayed offered, until the run's deadline.
+    """
+    monkeypatch.setenv('GITHUB_WORKFLOW', 'Pydantic AI Streaming Resilience Sweep')
+    sink = tmp_path / 'safeoutputs.jsonl'
+    monkeypatch.setenv('GH_AW_SAFE_OUTPUTS', str(sink))
+    noop_returns: list[str] = []
+    noop_offered: list[bool] = []
+
+    def noop(message: str) -> str:
+        if sink.exists():
+            error = McpError(ErrorData(code=-32602, message='calling "tools/call": E002: noop limit reached'))
+            raise ModelRetry(str(error)) from error
+        sink.write_text(json.dumps({'type': 'noop', 'message': message}) + '\n')
+        return 'ok'
+
+    def respond(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> ModelResponse:
+        noop_offered.append(any(tool_def.name == 'safeoutputs_noop' for tool_def in info.function_tools))
+        noop_returns.extend(
+            str(part.content)
+            for part in messages[-1].parts
+            if isinstance(part, ToolReturnPart) and part.tool_name == 'safeoutputs_noop'
+        )
+        if len(noop_returns) == 3:
+            return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart('done')])
+        return ModelResponse(parts=[ToolCallPart('safeoutputs_noop', {'message': 'progress note'})])
+
+    safe_outputs = FunctionToolset([noop]).prefixed('safeoutputs')
+    agent = workflow.build_agent()
+    with agent.override(model=streaming_model(respond)):
+        result = await agent.run('Sweep', toolsets=[safe_outputs], usage_limits=UsageLimits(request_limit=400))
+    assert result.output == 'done'
+    assert noop_returns[0] == 'ok'
+    assert (
+        noop_returns[1:]
+        == [
+            'error: calling "tools/call": E002: noop limit reached. '
+            'The earlier calls are already recorded, so do not call this tool again.'
+        ]
+        * 2
+    )
+    # A call from memory is still answered after the first rejection stops offering the tool.
+    assert noop_offered == [True, True, False, False]
+

+async def test_deadline_reports_time_limit_without_waiting(
+    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
+) -> None:
+    """A positive deadline cancels an active headless stream and reports its cause."""
+    budget = 1234
+    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, 'run_timeout_secs', lambda: budget)
+    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+    original_call_later = loop.call_later
+    callbacks: list[Callable[[], object]] = []
+    stream_stopped = False
+
+    def schedule(
+        delay: float, callback: Callable[..., object], *args: object, context: Context | None = None
+    ) -> asyncio.TimerHandle:
+        if delay == budget:
+            callbacks.append(partial(callback, *args))
+            return loop.call_at(loop.time() + budget, callback, *args, context=context)
+        return original_call_later(delay, callback, *args, context=context)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(loop, 'call_later', schedule)
+
+    async def pending_response(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
+        del messages, info
+        nonlocal stream_stopped
+        assert len(callbacks) == 1
+        callbacks[0]()
+        try:
+            await asyncio.Future()
+        finally:
+            stream_stopped = True
+        yield 'Unreachable'
+
+    agent = workflow.build_agent()
+    with agent.override(model=FunctionModel(stream_function=pending_response)):
+        result = await run_headless(
+            text='Investigate',
+            settings=Settings(request_limit=400, code_mode=False),
+            store=SettingsStore(tmp_path / 'clai2.db'),
+            project=ProjectSettings(),
+            agent=agent,
+        )
+    assert result == 1
+    assert stream_stopped
+    artifact = tmp_path / 'agent-stdio.log'
+    artifact.write_text(capsys.readouterr().err)
+    result = health.parse_run_result(artifact)
+    assert result is not None
+    assert result.failure == health.Failure('time_limit', None, None)
+    canonical = tmp_path / 'agent-session.jsonl'
+    canonical.write_text(
+        json.dumps({'type': 'session.result', 'data': {'status': 'failure', 'metadata': workflow.result_metadata}})

+'use strict';

+const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
+const fs = require('node:fs');
+const path = require('node:path');
+const { test } = require('node:test');
+
+const source = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, '../workflows/shared/engine-zai.md'), 'utf8');
+const body = source.split('      script: |\n')[1].split('\nsafe-outputs:')[0]
+  .split('\n').map(line => line.replace(/^ {8}/, '')).join('\n');
+const execute = new (Object.getPrototypeOf(async function () {}).constructor)('require', 'process', 'fetch', 'core', body);
+
+async function forward(content, regular = true) {
+  const sent = [];
+  const endpoints = [{ url: 'https://collector.invalid', headers: 'host-only' }];
+  let closed = false;
+  let removed = false;
+  const files = {
+    constants: fs.constants,
+    existsSync: () => content !== undefined,
+    openSync: (filename, flags) => {
+      assert.equal(filename, '/tmp/gh-aw/pydantic-ai-private-otel.jsonl');
+      assert.equal(flags, fs.constants.O_RDONLY | fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW | fs.constants.O_NONBLOCK);
+      return 3;
+    },
+    fstatSync: () => ({ isFile: () => regular }),
+    readFileSync: descriptor => { assert.equal(descriptor, 3); return content; },
+    closeSync: descriptor => { assert.equal(descriptor, 3); closed = true; },
+    unlinkSync: () => { removed = true; },
+  };
+  let error;
+  try {
+    await execute(name => {
+      if (name === 'fs') return files;
+      if (name === 'path') return path;
+      assert.equal(name, '/runner/gh-aw/actions/send_otlp_span.cjs');
+      return {
+        parseOTLPEndpoints: () => endpoints,
+        parseOTLPHeaders: value => { assert.equal(value, 'host-only'); return { Authorization: value }; },
+      };
+    }, { env: { RUNNER_TEMP: '/runner' } }, async (url, options) => {
+      assert.equal(url, 'https://collector.invalid/v1/traces');
+      assert.equal(options.method, 'POST');
+      assert.equal(options.headers.Authorization, 'host-only');
+      sent.push(JSON.parse(options.body));
+      return { ok: true, status: 200 };
+    }, { warning: () => assert.fail('unexpected export failure') });
+  } catch (caught) {
+    error = caught;
+  }
+  return { sent, closed, removed, error };
+}
+
+test('private workflow spans use host destinations without an artifact mirror', async () => {
+  const messages = JSON.stringify({ content: 'private probe '.repeat(400) });
+  const payload = { resourceSpans: [{ scopeSpans: [{ spans: [{ name: 'invoke_agent', traceId: '1'.repeat(32),
+    attributes: [{ key: 'gen_ai.input.messages', value: { stringValue: messages } }] }] }] }] };
+  const result = await forward(JSON.stringify(payload) + '\n');
+  assert.deepEqual(result, { sent: [payload], closed: true, removed: true, error: undefined });
+});
+
+test('missing spans after a noop are a no-op', async () => {
+  assert.deepEqual(await forward(undefined), { sent: [], closed: false, removed: false, error: undefined });
+});
+
+test('invalid diagnostic input is removed without exporting it', async () => {
+  const result = await forward('{"notResourceSpans":[]}');
+  assert.equal(result.sent.length, 0);
+  assert.equal(result.closed, true);
+  assert.equal(result.removed, true);

+});

signature: function withParser<T extends SomeType>(schema: T, parser: (input: unknown) => core.output<T> | INVALID): T
docstring:
Install an already-generated parser as a schema's fast path. Returns a clone; the original is
unchanged.

The parser takes the input and returns the parsed value, or `INVALID` to hand the parse to the
runtime. It must be synchronous and forward-direction, and it must build fresh output rather than
return its input — Zod cannot check either, and a wrong *success* is returned to the caller as-is.

`compile()` is the ordinary entry point. This is for a build-time or native compiler that produces
a parser where `new Function` is unavailable.
